rule: Naming is a base family with a descriptive prefix (Giant, Ice, Poison, Jungle, Dark) and numbered variant keys (man, man2, man3; guard1, guard2). Map labels are name, x, z and a size class 0-2, with a slash that the client may draw as a line break (client not read). Signs are a name plus one functional line, with a shop sign taking a name and a trade line. Faction is by zone and by NPC category, not one global map. Rumours are dialogue topics the player picks from a menu; the chosen answer is a breadcrumb that names the next NPC. A zone voice is three lines: a world rule, an identity, and a one-way gate with a teleport on exit.
keep: Sign as a name plus one functional line, placed at junctions
Map label with a size class and an optional two-line split
Rumour as a player-chosen dialogue topic whose answer routes to the next NPC

look_test: Build one zone entrance with the three-line zone voice and one junction sign in the same style, then compare it on a 375-wide phone against a current Pit zone label. Dom checks that the sign reads in one glance, that the three lines place the zone, and that the one-way line makes him pause before stepping through. Compare a two-line slash label against a single-line label for readability.
licence_note: Code MIT (LICENSE line 1; README.md line 62). Game-derived content (names, dialogue, signs, quest text) has no licence line and no source statement in the repo (AU002). Class C. Dialogue cites a commercial game by name in places; treat as category-level only. Structures (one-way gate, rumour topic, size-class label) are generic; donor lines and names are not reused.
